Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:43: And further, the matter is explained more in the Tikkunim (beginning of page 61), in these words: and therefore the time for marital relations of Torah scholars is on the Sabbath - for on the weekdays, when Metatron rules (Ezekiel 46:1), "it shall be closed the six working days" - in it, the gate is closed; and on the Sabbath day the gate shall open and the Shechinah shall go forth from it to be united with her husband - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:44: And in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 78a) he explained the verse (Leviticus 18:16 - actually verse referencing daughter-in-law's nakedness), "you shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law," concerning a Torah scholar on weekdays, that he should not approach his "daughter-in-law," who is his wife, in these words: "kallah" [bride/daughter-in-law] in a supernal secret is to show that whoever blemishes below blemishes above, for we have learned that the time for marital relations of Torah scholars is from Sabbath to Sabbath, because they know the secret of the matter and direct their hearts, and their will is found complete, and because they beget, they are called sons of the King - and if these blemish the matter below, it is as though they blemish the "bride" above, then it is written, "you shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law" - this is because they know the ways of the Torah; the rest of the people, that is what "your daughter-in-law" literally uncovered means, and through this sin the Shechinah withdraws from them - to this point. Behold, it is explained that the obligation upon a Torah scholar is to separate from his wife on weekdays, because they have the union of the Shechinah, which is through the occupation with Torah - and the rest of the people, who do not look to ascend in the virtue of Torah and to be Torah scholars and to be united with the Shechinah, cause the Shechinah to withdraw from them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:45: And further, they elaborated in the Zohar (Parashat Yitro, page 89b) on the virtue of the marital time of Torah scholars from Sabbath to Sabbath, on the verse (Isaiah 56:4), "to the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths" - and on the punishment of the common people who do not conduct themselves so, and it calls the children of the common people "children of harlotry," because they do not practice the fitting holiness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:46: Therefore every person is obligated to add, every day, Torah and service, until he attains the level of a Torah scholar, and merits to be united with the Shechinah and to be among her servants who draw near to her, sanctified with her holiness. And therefore our holy Torah, in Parashat Kedoshim, at the beginning of the exposition, explains how the matters of holiness are, and says (Leviticus 19:3), "every man, you shall fear your mother and your father, and you shall keep My Sabbaths" - and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained, in interpreting the verse (Parashat Kedoshim, page 82a), that these are the Torah scholars who "castrate" themselves the whole six weekdays to occupy themselves with Torah, and he said that the word "tishmoru" [you shall keep/guard] is like (Genesis 37:11), "and his father kept [guarded] the matter."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:47: And reason dictates that whoever does not rise does not desire the love of the Shechinah at all - for the lover who follows his beloved does not slumber or sleep from the abundance of his love for her. And since this Torah scholar does not rise, the Shechinah will complain of him that he has no love for her, for he neglects her appointed time and does not care for her - and the Holy One, blessed be He, too, will complain of him that he neglects the appointed time of His daughter, who is the Torah - and the Torah has already been compared to a beautiful, beloved king's daughter, see the Zohar - and as it is said (Deuteronomy 33:4), "Moses commanded us a Torah, an inheritance," and so on - and they said, of blessed memory, in Pesachim (49b), Rabbi Chiya taught, whoever occupies himself with Torah before an ignorant person [am ha'aretz] is as though he had relations with his betrothed before him, as it is said, "Moses commanded us a Torah [morashah], an inheritance" - do not read "morashah" but "me'orasah" [betrothed].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:48: And concerning this they said in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 207a) that David would sleep sixty breaths, so that when midnight came he would rise, and the Shechinah would not find him sleeping, being bound to the Other Side, in these words: and therefore King David would measure the measure of the night, so that he would be sustained in life, that the taste of death not rule over him, and when the night was divided, David would be sustained in his place - because when midnight is aroused and the holy crown is aroused, He wished not to find David bound in another place, the place of death - for when the night is divided and supernal holiness is aroused, and a person sleeps on his bed and does not awaken to attend to the glory of his Master, behold he is bound in the secret of death and attached to another place. And therefore King David would stand to attend to the glory of his Master constantly, life facing life, and would not sleep in slumber unto the taste of death, and therefore he would doze like a horse, sixty breaths, and not fully - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:49: Behold, that at midnight the supernal holiness is aroused, and the Shechinah is aroused and sends the souls below so that they be aroused for the honor of their Maker - and whoever is aroused and does not rise does not attend to the honor of his Maker; and the honor of the Shechinah, that a person be aroused for her through the Torah, which is the Tree of Life, and through this she is united through the eighteen worlds - and this is "life facing life," along the lines explained in the Zohar (Parashat Emor, page 90a), "the righteous shall inherit the land" (Psalms 37:9), that at midnight the Shechinah is between two righteous ones, the supernal Righteous One and the lower righteous one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:50: And in the Zohar (Parashat Bamidbar, page 119a), that the Holy One, blessed be He, restores the souls to Israel at midnight so that they occupy themselves with Torah, in these words: and should you say, behold, there are many people who awaken at night while the tree of death still rules, that tree of death does its work - why? Because it is written (Psalms 14:2), "to see if there is any who is wise, who seeks God" - and let there be no opening of the mouth for a person to say, had I not ruled over my soul, I would have striven in Torah at night - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:51: Behold, the restoration of the soul at midnight includes both the ignorant person and the Torah scholar - and if it were not incumbent upon the ignorant person too to rise and occupy himself with Torah, why would the Holy One, blessed be He, send back his soul? Rather, certainly it is so that a person take it to heart and say, the Holy One, blessed be He, did not restore my soul to me at this hour for nothing, but so that I occupy myself with Torah. And every single day he should add, for they said (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 13), "and whoever does not add, subtracts" - the reason being that if he does not add, he dries up, and is found to be like a tree that produces no fruit and has no use except to be burned - and so is the teaching of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Tikkunim (page 87a), in these words: woe to those people who do not strive in Torah, who are called dry trees, destined to be burned in the fire of Gehinnom - and it was not for nothing that the masters of the mishnah established that they toil and inherit Gehinnom - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:52: Further, concerning the punishment of one who does not rise, and the reward if he does rise, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 23a), in these words: Rabbi Yosi opened and said (Job 35:10), "and none says, where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night" - come and see, at the time the north wind is aroused and the night is divided, they have already established that one flame goes out and strikes beneath the wings of the rooster, and it strikes its wings and calls, and that flame, when it reaches and is aroused toward it, gazes at it and shudders and calls and stops, and attends, for the honor of its Master, to do His will, and calls to the people - and therefore it is called "sekhvi," attentive - and is called "gever" [mighty one/rooster] because it is aroused by the flame of Gevurah, from the side of Gevurah it comes to be aroused in the world - then those people of faith stand and give strength to the Community of Israel, and this is then called "the song of Torah," and therefore David inherited kingship, he and his sons forever and for all generations. And when the rooster calls and people lie on their beds and do not awaken, the rooster calls again and says what it says, and this has been established: at dawn it strikes its wings, woe to so-and-so, rebuked by his Master, forsaken by his Master, that his spirit was not aroused and he did not attend to the honor of his Master. When day dawns, a herald calls out concerning him and says, and none says, "where is God my Maker, who gives" - the word "gives" [songs in the night] is to assist him with those praises and to be all in one assistance - it should have said "oseini" [my Maker, singular for me]; what is "oseini" [rather "oseinu", "our Maker"]? Rather, at the time a person rises at midnight and strives in song, for "song of Torah" is called only [song] at night, and when he is found in Torah as day dawns, the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel prepare him with one thread of Chesed, to save him from everything and to illuminate him among the higher and lower beings - to this point, relevant here. And Rabbi Abba explained there concerning "oseinu," that the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel prepare him and make him a new creature every day, as it is said (Psalms 149:2), "let Israel rejoice in its Makers."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:53: Behold, from the teaching it appears how great the reward is for one who rises at midnight to occupy himself with Torah, and likewise his punishment if he does not rise - for it says that the supernal herald calls him "rebuked by his Master," and so on, "that his spirit was not aroused and he did not attend to the honor of his Master." And it says "his spirit was not aroused," because the soul comes to a person at midnight, as explained in the previous teaching from Parashat Bamidbar - except that when the soul comes to him, his spirit must be aroused to rise, to give honor to his Creator, to occupy himself with Torah, and not be lazy in a manner that he returns to sleep, as it is said (Proverbs 19:15), "laziness casts into a deep sleep" - but rather he should rise with alacrity to His blessed service, for the arousal of the spirit indicates alacrity, like the king's servants who serve their master with alacrity to find favor in his eyes, and are seen by all to have their deeds done with great alacrity and much love, so that the king know their good heart toward him and elevate and exalt them - and by how much more is it fitting that we hasten to the service of our King and Creator, to find favor before Him, that He forgive our sins and that our Torah be pleasing before Him, that we be called His servants - for it is explained in Parashat Vayikra (Zohar, page 13a) that the psalm (Psalms 134:1), "behold, bless the LORD, all servants of the LORD," is said of those who stand to occupy themselves with Torah from midnight onward - and certainly it is not fitting to call one "servant of the LORD" except one who is complete in every kind of service, and that the service be exclusively for Him, blessed be He, without any ulterior motive - for if there is any ulterior motive for that service, that motive is found to be the cause of the service, and once the cause is nullified, the service is nullified, and this is not called serving the LORD.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:54: And along these lines, if a person rises early to read Torah at midnight in order to attain one of the virtues that Rashbi, peace be upon him, wrote in his book - to attain wisdom, or that his livelihood be provided for him, as explained in Parashat Emor (page 90a) on the verse (Psalms 111:5), "He has given food [teref] to those who fear Him," said of those occupied with Torah from midnight onward - and the many other virtues written in the Zohar - it is found that these motives are the cause of his reading Torah, and this is like one who studies in order to be called "Rav" and to be called "Rabbi."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:55: And Rashbi, peace be upon him, needed to write all those virtues, along the lines that our holy Torah needed to write the reward of the commandments in this world in the passage "if you walk in My statutes" (Leviticus 26:4), "then I will give your rains in their season," and so on - and this is so that from [performing the commandments] not for their own sake one comes to [performing them] for their own sake.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:56: And further, it is possible to say that the intent of our holy Torah in mentioning the reward of the commandments is to say that in our performing the commandments for the sake of Heaven, and in our unifying His supernal attributes properly, this reward will follow in any case, both in this world and in the World to Come - for according to how the soul arouses above, the flow from the supernal one necessarily gives it its portion from what it repaired. And so too the matter for one who occupies himself with Torah from midnight onward - for he attains all those virtues from what he has done, and they are not external virtues that have no relation to the deed, Heaven forfend, but rather all those virtues are related to the deed and are drawn from it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:57: And therefore the wise person should take to heart to perform his service for the sake of Heaven, without any ulterior motive, for He who examines hearts and thoughts knows whether his service is pleasing and clean before Him or not - for when the Holy One, blessed be He, sees, with His supernal eye of providence, that a person's service is not fitting before Him, He places a stumbling block before him so that the virtues Rashbi, peace be upon him, wrote do not come to be for him, in order to push him away from being called one of the servants of the LORD, and to test whether his service is constant before Him or not - and through this a distinction is made between one who serves God and one who does not serve Him: if he serves in order to receive a reward, if the reward were nullified his service would be nullified; but one who serves in order not to receive a reward, his service is forever constant and is never nullified for any reason - and he is called a servant of the LORD, not a servant of the reward. And so it is fitting to be called one who occupies himself with Torah for its own sake, as explained - that he occupies himself with it only to do the will of his Maker.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:58: By this Rabbi Yosi, peace be upon him, taught, in the teaching before us that we copied from Parashat Vayikra, when Rabbi Yosi said that that flame that comes from above, from the side of Gevurah, and from the side of the angel Gabriel, who is the supernal herald that gives six voices, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Parashat Shelach Lecha, end of page 171b) - it strikes the wings of the rooster, and it shudders and gazes and attends, for the honor of its Master, to do His will, and calls to the people, and therefore it is called "sekhvi," attentive - and he explained that just as the supernal herald is for the supernal souls, that they stand for the service of the Creator to occupy themselves with Torah, so that until midnight each one is occupied with Torah and reflects within himself on what he was occupied with during the day, so the lower herald calls to the lower people.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:59: And so they explained there (the aforementioned page): from after midnight, the flame of the pillar of Isaac goes out and strikes this rooster, who is called "gever," in the manner that another supernal "gever" [is] over it - once this "gever" strikes it, it calls and gives six voices, all with understanding. When it calls, all the roosters of this world call, and another flame goes out from it and reaches them beneath their wings, and they call - what does it call? At the first hour it calls and says (Psalms 29:4), "the voice of the LORD is with power, the voice of the LORD is with majesty"; at the second hour it calls and says (Micah 6:9), "the LORD's voice calls to the city"; at the third hour it calls and says (Psalms 29:7), "the voice of the LORD hews flames of fire"; at the fourth hour it calls and says (ibid. 29:8), "the voice of the LORD shakes the wilderness"; at the fifth hour it calls and says (ibid. 29:3), "the voice of the LORD is upon the waters," and so on; at the sixth hour it calls and says (ibid. 29:9), "the voice of the LORD makes the hinds calve," and so on. Afterward it calls and says (Isaiah 40:6), "a voice says, call! And he says, what shall I call?" and so on - and this is the rooster that calls and does not cease, and afterward it calls as before - and what does it call? All the deeds of the people of the world, because it is the master of the "machamta" [scale] and the scribe's inkhorn is on its loins, and it writes down all the deeds of people every day, and at night, after it has called all these calls, it calls out everything it wrote during the day - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:60: Behold, it is explicit that the supernal herald calls him "rebuked," and this herald is called Gabriel, as explained at the end of his words, that the scribe's inkhorn is on his loins, and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Shabbat 55a) that this is said of Gabriel. And he says, "when it calls, all the roosters of this world call" - and so it is also explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayishlach, page 172b), where it says there concerning midnight, and the herald stands firm and calls loudly and proclaims - then how many are those who arrange song and perform service. And it says there afterward, and they sing until dawn rises. And so in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, end of page 21), it explains that at the beginning of the night all the gates are locked and all the holy ones sit silent, and the external forces spread through the world, and it says, when the night is divided, the herald stands and proclaims, and gates are opened, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:61: Now, when the wise person considers and takes these things to heart, it is fitting that his spirit be aroused and that he hasten to give honor to his Creator upon hearing the voice of the rooster, which is the lower herald drawn from the supernal herald - just as the supernal beings are aroused upon hearing the voice of the supernal herald to give honor to their Creator - and he should think in his mind: were he in the palace of a king and heard the voice of the king's herald calling his servants to stand for the king's service, how he would rise with alacrity, fearing lest he be punished - so why should he not fear upon hearing the voice of the rooster, since those who know the hidden things have explained to us that it calls with the power of the supernal herald, and it is fitting that he fear lest the bonds of his debts be called out before Him and he be punished - for it was said that after six hours, which is the time of the rising of the pillar of dawn, then it calls out all the deeds written during the day - and if a person is then occupied with Torah, the Torah is worthy to pass over his transgressions, until he repents. And further, one who rises at night to occupy himself with Torah - the Torah informs him of his sin so that he repent, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 23b) on the verse (Leviticus 4:23), "or his sin, which he has sinned, is made known to him" - but if he is then asleep, what can he answer for his sins? Certainly he deserves punishment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:62: And so Rabbi Elazar, peace be upon him, explained in the Zohar (beginning of Parashat Metzora), in these words: Rabbi Elazar opened (Ecclesiastes 9:12), "like fish caught in an evil net, and like birds caught in a snare, so are the sons of men snared" - this verse has already been explained, but come and see, people do not know, do not hear, and do not observe the will of their Master, and a herald calls out concerning them every day, and there is none who heeds him. At the time night descends and the gates are closed, the hole of the great abyss is aroused, and how many bands of destroyers are found in the world - then the Holy One, blessed be He, casts sleep upon all the people of the world, even upon all those in whom there is an arousal of life, and they roam the world and inform people of things, some of them false and some true, and people are bound in sleep. When the north wind is aroused and the night is divided, a herald goes out, and the Holy One, blessed be He, enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous, and then His flames go out and strike beneath the wings of the rooster, and it calls, and all the people of the world stir on their beds, and there is none whose spirit is aroused for service. When morning comes, the herald calls, and all the hosts and camps above praise the Holy One, blessed be He - this is what is written (Job 38:7), "when the morning stars sang together" - then how many gates open on every side, and the gate of Abraham opens, through the Community of Israel, to invite all the people of the world - this is what is written (Genesis 21:33), "and he planted a tamarisk in Beer Sheba" - and there is none whose spirit is aroused in service to his Master - in what face shall he stand before the King when they arouse judgment against him and seize him by the collar, and no merit is found for him to be saved - then it is written, "and like birds caught in a snare, so are the sons of men snared" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:63: Behold, a person is held accountable in judgment if he awakened from his sleep at midnight and did not rise to read Torah, and the punishment is great when day dawns and he does not rise to praise his Maker in the morning prayer.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:64: And so in the Chupat Eliyahu it says, in these words: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says, over three things the Holy One, blessed be He, weeps: over a Torah scholar who has no bread in his basket, and over a Torah scholar who does not occupy himself with Torah in the last watch, of whom the verse says (Proverbs 26:14), "the door turns on its hinge, and the lazy man on his bed," and over one who is proud for no reason - to this point. And the matter of this weeping over a Torah scholar who does not occupy himself with Torah in the last watch is because the essence of Torah in a scholar is to give honor to the One who gave him the Torah, and if he does not give honor to the Torah, the Torah is found in him almost in vain - and therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, complains of him, that He gave him the Torah, which is His daughter, and he does not treat her properly, as shall be explained further.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:65: And so it is proven in several places in the Zohar that the essence of rising early to read Torah is to bind night with day - and so it appears in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 4a), that one voice is aroused in the Garden of Eden and says, who among you looks forward every day to the light that shines when the King commands the doe [dawn], and the King is honored above all the kings of the world? Whoever does not anticipate this every day, in that world he has no portion here - to this point. And my teacher, peace be upon him, explained that the reality of this illumination that shines "when the King commands the doe" is at the time the pillar of dawn rises, as explained in the Zohar (ibid., Parashat Beshalach, page 46a), in these words: and when morning comes, the Community of Israel comes and delights in the Holy One, blessed be He, and He extends to her the scepter of Chesed, and it does not ascend alone but ascends together with those who are joined with her - and this has been said, as it is written (Psalms 42:9), "by day the LORD commands His kindness, and in the night," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:66: And there, at the end of the column, are the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in these words: when the night ends and morning comes, and it darkens and grows dim, then the King and the Matronita are in the secret of joy, and He gives her gifts, and to all the members of His palace - happy is the portion of whoever is counted in the number - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:67: And so it is further explained there (Zohar, beginning of Parashat Pinchas), in these words: Rabbi Shimon said, as it were, all those who merit to strive in Torah from when the night is divided and come to be with the Matronita - when day dawns, to receive the face of the King, he is strengthened and takes possession in the Shechinah, and not only that, but Chesed rests upon him, as we have established - to this point. And so they explained there (Parashat Miketz, page 194b), the verse (Psalms 147:11), "the LORD is pleased with those who fear Him, who hope for His kindness," concerning those who rise at midnight and wait until day to receive the thread of Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:68: Behold, from these teachings it appears the obligation incumbent upon one who occupies himself with Torah from midnight onward, to bind night with day - and so it is further explained there (Zohar, Parashat Vayikra, end of page 25a), in these words: and when the holy doe is aroused, descending in the north wind, that meritorious one who acquires her rises and is strengthened like a mighty lion in Torah until morning comes, and goes with that holy doe to appear before the King to receive one thread of Chesed - to this point. Behold, it is explained more clearly. And they say, "and that meritorious one who acquires her rises" - my teacher, peace be upon him, explained a great matter in these words, that the rising at midnight must be to bind oneself to the Shechinah, like a person jealous for his wife, who does not want her love to separate from him, and there is pleasure only from the side of love - so the righteous man is jealous, not wanting the Shechinah to separate from him and abandon him and her love to separate from him, and therefore, from the abundance of love he has for her, he rises to do her will, to occupy himself with Torah, for through the occupation with Torah he unites with her - and without doubt, whoever rises to occupy himself with Torah with this desire of love mentioned will not fall asleep, and for this Rashbi, peace be upon him, said in his words, "and is strengthened like a mighty lion until morning comes."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:69: And one who rises at midnight is the pattern of the supernal Righteous One [Yesod] for the secret of union - and so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Emor, page 90a) on the verse (Psalms 111:5), "He has given food to those who fear Him," in these words: what is "He has given food to those who fear Him"? Rather, as it is written (Proverbs 31:15), "she rises while it is still night and gives food to her household" - from here we learn that whoever labors in Torah at night, and rises at midnight, at the hour when the Community of Israel is aroused to prepare the house for the King, and this one joins with her, this one is called "master of the house," and they give him every day some of the preparations of the house - this is what is written, "and gives food to her household and a portion to her maidens" - who is "her household"? All those who join with her at night are called "her household," members of her household - and therefore "He has given food to those who fear Him" - what is "teref" [food]? Real food, that is taken from a distant supernal place, as it is written (ibid. 31:14), "she brings her bread from afar" - and who merits this food? The end of the verse proves it, as it is written, "he shall remember His covenant forever" - whoever strives in Torah to join with her at night; and not only that, but the Holy One, blessed be He, has one supernal Righteous One, and he joins with Him, and the two of them together inherit for the Community of Israel (Isaiah 60:21), "and the righteous shall inherit the land" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:70: And the reason that those who rise at midnight merit the secret of the "food" mentioned in the teaching is because it is measure for measure - just as they cause the drawing of blessings from the holy place, as it is written (Psalms 134:2), "lift up your hands in holiness," as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 13a) - so it is fitting that their sustenance be given to them from there. And from the positive you infer the negative. Behold, it is explained, the great virtue that one who occupies himself with Torah from midnight onward, binding night with day, has.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:71: And so they further explained in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 130b), that there is praise for the morning prayer when a person joins to it the Torah of his nighttime occupation - it says there that when morning time arrives, then the herald comes early and calls, prepare yourselves, supernal holy ones who praise your Master, prepare yourselves with the praises of day - then day is separated from night. Happy is the portion of one who rises from the praises of Torah in which he labored at night, at that time, for the morning prayer - to this point. And so it is also explained concerning its virtue at the beginning of Parashat Va'etchanan (page 260a) - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:72: And just as the reward is great, so the punishment is great for one who does not rise, as explained - and they explained this matter in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, end of page 21), in these words: when the night is divided, the herald stands and proclaims, and gates open - then one spirit from the north side is aroused and strikes David's harp, and it plays of itself and sings praise to the King, and the Holy One, blessed be He, delights with the righteous in the Garden of Eden. Happy is the portion of whoever is aroused at that time and strives in Torah - and whoever stands at that time is called a companion of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Community of Israel, and not only that, but these are called brothers and friends to Him, as it is written (Psalms 122:8), "for the sake of my brothers and friends, I will now say, peace be within you" - they are called companions, as it is written (Song of Songs 8:13), "companions listen for your voice." When day comes, the herald stands and proclaims, and the gates of the south side open, and stars and constellations are aroused, and the gates of mercy open, and the King sits and receives praises - then the Community of Israel and all those companions take hold of her wings, and their words come and rest in the bosom of the King - then the King commands, and they write in a book all those members of His household, and a thread of Chesed is drawn upon them, for by that thread a person is crowned with the crown of the King, and through it the higher and lower beings fear him - and even at the time when the masters of judgment stand to judge the world, he enters all the gates of the King, and there is none to stop his hand, and those masters of judgment do not judge him with judgment. Happy is the portion of the righteous who strive in Torah, and all the more so at the time the King desires the words of Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:73: Come and see the secret of the matter: the Community of Israel stands before the King only through Torah, for as long as Israel were in the land and strove in Torah, the Community of Israel rested with them; when they were idle from the words of Torah, she could not remain with them a single hour. Therefore, at the time the Community of Israel is aroused toward the King, her host is strengthened, and holy kings see fit to receive them; and whenever the Community of Israel comes to the King and Torah is not found with her, as it were her strength weakens - woe to those who weaken her strength above. Therefore happy are those who strive in Torah, and all the more so at that hour when the Community of Israel needs it - then the Holy One, blessed be He, calls concerning him (Isaiah 49:3), "and He said to me, you are My servant, Israel, in whom I am glorified" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:74: Behold, it is explained in this teaching the obligation upon us to occupy ourselves with Torah from midnight onward, for through this we give strength to the Shechinah through the arousal of Torah - for then the Holy One, blessed be He, desires the words of Torah, and then the Shechinah says, "companions listen for your voice, let me hear it," as explained at the beginning of Parashat Pinchas. And whoever does not rise, and does not attend to give strength and arousal to the Shechinah, weakens, Heaven forfend, the supernal power, as it is written, "as it were her strength weakens, and woe to those who weaken the strength above."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:75: And similar to this he explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayishlach, page 174b) on the verse (Proverbs 24:10), "if you faint in the day of adversity, your strength is small" - concerning one who slackens his hands from occupying himself with Torah, in these words: what is "if you faint"? Whoever's hands slacken from the Holy One, blessed be He, not to strengthen himself in Him - and how does a person strengthen himself in the Holy One, blessed be He? Whoever strengthens himself in Torah - for whoever strengthens himself in Torah strengthens himself in the Tree of Life, and as it were gives strength to the Community of Israel to be strengthened. And if he slackens from Torah, what is written? "If you faint" - if he slackens from Torah "in the day of adversity, your strength is small" - on the day trouble comes to him, as it were he distresses the Shechinah, who is the strength of the world. And this explanation is "your strength is small [tzar ko'ach]" - like "tzar Kaf-Heh" [distresses the Heh] - and so he explains further there. And the reason is that once Samael comes to accuse him, and the Shechinah has no defending face to answer for him, she stands in distress and sorrow, and her strength is contracted, and she does not give her strength to the lower beings, Israel her children, as fitting.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:76: And he further explained there another interpretation of "your strength is small" - come and see, at the time a person slackens from Torah and walks in an unfit path, how many adversaries are ready for him to become his accusers on the day of trouble, and even a person's own soul, which is his strength and power, becomes his adversary against him, as it is written, "tzar ko'ach" - because it becomes "tzar," an adversary, against him - to this point. And this explanation is "your strength is small," that his soul, which is his strength, is an adversary and enemy to him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:77: And it appears to me that without doubt, whoever rises at midnight and his intent and desire is to give strength to the Shechinah out of love for her - along the lines of (Isaiah 62:6), "you who remind the LORD, take no rest" - as explained in Parashat Vaera (page 30a) - strength shall be poured into his soul, enabling him to fast, for they said in the Zohar, which we copied above, that they make him a new creature, and certainly strength is renewed in his soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:78: And I see how many of the penitents rise at midnight and occupy themselves with Torah until day, and fast - and all this is divine help upon them, for "man does not live by bread alone." And if not, just as he weakens the supernal power, the strength of his soul is weakened - and these matters are clear, and we elaborated on this in the Gate of Repentance, chapter 6.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:79: And the reason for this is that the night is given for the occupation with Torah, as they said (Shemot Rabbah 47:5; Vayikra Rabbah 19:1; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:10), "there is no song of Torah except at night" - the intent being from midnight onward, for then it is called "lailah" [night]; before midnight it is called "leil," as explained in the Tikkunim - in these words, there in the Zohar (Parashat Beshalach, page 46a): Rabbi Yosi opened, "for the leader, on the morning doe, a psalm of David" - how beloved is the Torah before the Holy One, blessed be He, for whoever strives in Torah is beloved above, beloved below, the Holy One, blessed be He, listens to his words, does not forsake him in this world and does not forsake him in the World to Come. And one needs to labor in Torah by day and by night - why? So that he be found close to the complete holy Name - for just as there is no day without night, and it is not complete except one with the other, so one must be found with the Torah day and night, to be a completion for a person, day and night - and this has been said, that the essence of night is from midnight onward, and although the first half is included in the general category of night, nevertheless at midnight the Holy One, blessed be He, enters the Garden of Eden to delight with the righteous, and then a person must rise and labor in Torah - and this has been said, that the Holy One, blessed be He, and all the righteous, all heed it - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:80: And in the Tikkunim (page 2) it says that from midnight onward it is called "lailah," in these words: masters of Torah from the side of the central pillar - for at midnight David would rise to join himself with the Shechinah, called "night" [laylah], and he is "the watchman, what of the night" (Isaiah 21:11) - "leyl" [belonging to] the LORD, "a night of watching for the LORD" - and therefore it is said, whoever occupies himself with Torah at night, the Holy One, blessed be He, draws upon him a thread of Chesed by day, as it is said (Psalms 42:9), "by day the LORD commands His kindness, and in the night His song is with me" - to this point. Behold, our intent is explicitly explained. And likewise what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, "whoever occupies himself with Torah at night, the Holy One, blessed be He, draws upon him," and so on - the intent is concerning its aspect called "night," which is from midnight onward, and so it is also explained in the teaching we copied above from Parashat Vayikra (end of page 21).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:81: And from this teaching that we copied from the Tikkunim, it appears explicitly that they are not called "masters of Torah," who correspond to the attribute of Jacob, except those who occupy themselves with it from midnight onward, as it says, "from the side of the central pillar, for at midnight David would rise to join himself with his Shechinah." And the reason Rashbi needed to say this matter is to explain the word "masters of Torah," whose wording in the holy tongue is "ba'al Torah" [master/possessor of Torah] - and behold, concerning the pious ones and the mighty ones, who correspond to Chesed and Gevurah, he has already explained the reason above; but the reason for those occupied with Torah, that they be called "possessors of Torah" and not merely "those occupied with Torah," and he answered that it is because they unite the attribute of Torah with night, for so David would do, rising at midnight to join himself with his Shechinah through the occupation with Torah - and especially in light of what they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 92b) concerning "at midnight I will rise to give thanks to You," the matter is settled well.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:82: And this is the matter of occupying oneself with Torah for its own sake [lishmah], which they explained in the Tikkunim (page 2a), that the intent is to unify the Holy One, blessed be He, the Name YHVH, with the Shechinah - and this is "lishmah," for the sake of the Name [leshem Hashem].
